_comment: Real, measured tokens/sec from actual generation runs (not estimates). Machine: Apple M4 Pro, 48GB, macOS 26.5.2. Collected during development of this tool -- see README for methodology.

measurements.notes: MoE, 3B active/30B total, no thinking mode; updated to a 10-trial mean (std 0.66, 0.73% relative) via mlx_lm.generate, 100 generated tokens/trial -- first repeated-trial noise-floor measurement in this project's own data, confirms run-to-run noise is well under 1%, not the 1.8-3.5% a later research pass claimed without measuring it

MoE, 4B active/26B total. Original 76.7 value (kept no other provenance than 'thinking mode enabled') replaced with a rigorous 10-trial mean via mlx_lm.generate (std 0.60, 0.76% relative, tightly clustered 78.46-79.93), taken while re-investigating this project's own persistently-worst calibration point. The corrected value alone dropped this point's formula error from +6.3% (using the old, apparently stale/less-rigorous 76.7) to +3.2% -- suggesting most of what looked like a real unexplained residual (attributed to MoE-width bandwidth effects in formula-accuracy-gap.md item 5/8) was actually just an imprecise original measurement, not a formula problem.
MoE hybrid (Gated DeltaNet + attention), thinking mode by default; updated to a 10-trial mean (std 0.71, 0.80% relative) via mlx_lm.generate, 100 generated tokens/trial
MoE, 4 active experts/32 total, mixed 4/8-bit OptiQ quant
dense LFM2 hybrid (10 ShortConv layers + 6 attention layers, 16 total), via mlx_lm.generate, 20 prompt + 71 generated tokens
LFM2 MoE hybrid (ShortConv + attention + routed experts), via mlx_lm.generate, 20 prompt + 120 generated tokens
IBM Granite hybrid (Mamba-2 + attention + MoE), via mlx_lm.generate, 19 prompt + 107 generated tokens
Nemotron-H single-component-per-layer (Mamba-2/attention/MLP/MoE via hybrid_override_pattern), 30B total, ~3B active, via mlx_lm.generate, 27 prompt + 131 generated tokens, peak memory 33.7GB

dense GatedDeltaNet hybrid (Qwen3.5, NO MoE -- first pure-dense GatedDeltaNet ground-truth point; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit above is GatedDeltaNet+MoE), 5-trial mean (std 2.3, 0.68% relative) via mlx_lm.generate, 100 generated tokens/trial. Also used to confirm probe_mlx.py's synthetic-probe deficit is far larger for GatedDeltaNet-hybrid architectures (~33-40% raw) than for dense/MoE (~15-19%) -- see docs/formula-accuracy-gap.md item 4

classic (non-hybrid) Mamba-1, 130M params, unquantized bf16, tied embeddings -- first pure-SSM ground-truth point (previously zero coverage: every other SSM-family point in this set is a hybrid). 5-trial mean (std 2.4, 0.49% relative) via mlx_lm.generate, 100 generated tokens/trial. Downloading and testing this real config also surfaced two real weight-count bugs, both fixed: (1) pure-SSM architectures (no num_attention_heads field at all) were falling through layer_kinds detection to generic 'full attention' and getting priced as 4*hidden*hidden blocks -- confirmed real params inflated from ~130M to 218.8M (+68%); (2) even after fixing detection, the generic per-layer loop still added a phantom dense MLP per layer, since mlx_lm.models.mamba.ResidualBlock has ONLY a mixer, no separate MLP at all (confirmed reading mamba.py directly) -- both fixed via ArchProfile.is_pure_ssm. A third, more general bug (tie_word_embeddings never read anywhere, confirmed via this repo's own safetensors index having no separate lm_head weight) was also found and fixed, affecting RAM sizing (not the speed formula, which already counted lm_head bytes once regardless of tying). This model itself is NOT included in probe_formula.py's speed-formula calibration set -- like Josiefied-Qwen3.5-0.8B above, it's small/fast enough (490.8 tok/s) to hit the same 'small/fast model breaks the global fixed-overhead term' problem (formula predicts 856.9, +74.6% error) -- see docs/formula-accuracy-gap.md item 7, now confirmed on a THIRD independent architecture family.

REAL Level-1 ground truth (not a probe_mlx.py estimate) for this project's original worst-known held-out model -- the one whose apparent +26-30% gap motivated the mixed-quantization-manifest and quantization-metadata bytes-per-token fixes (formula-accuracy-gap.md item 3b). 12-trial mean via mlx_lm.generate, 100 generated tokens/trial, all 12 trials tightly clustered 77.68-79.76, std 0.78 (0.98% relative) -- a genuinely clean measurement. (A first attempt at this same measurement, taken immediately after a fresh ~20GB download, showed severe cold-disk-cache instability in its first 5 trials, 4-6 tok/s, before jumping to steady-state -- re-run after the file was warm in the OS page cache; see formula-accuracy-gap.md item 4 for that methodological finding.) probe_formula.py predicts 79.5 tok/s against this -- +1.0% error, decisively confirming the original +26-30% gap was entirely a probe_mlx.py proxy artifact (its own hybrid-calibrated estimate for this exact model is 86.9, +10.4% over real), not a real formula error. Not added to the 9-point speed-formula calibration set (not needed -- the formula's near-perfect fit here is a genuine held-out validation, and folding it in would blur that distinction), but used to refine probe_mlx.py's own HYBRID_CALIBRATION_RATIO (0.63 -> 0.655, now fit from 3 real points instead of 2).

First real MLA (Multi-Head Latent Attention) ground-truth point in this project (2B params, non-DeepSeek). 10-trial mean via mlx_lm.generate, 100 generated tokens/trial, std 1.45 (0.88% relative). probe_formula.py predicts 192.9 -- +16.8% error, a real, unexplained residual. Source-verified this is NOT a weight-count bug: mlx_lm.models.youtu_llm.YoutuLLMAttention's q_a_proj/q_a_layernorm/q_b_proj, kv_a_proj_with_mqa/kv_a_layernorm/kv_b_proj, and o_proj structure matches this project's _mla_weight_params() formula term-for-term exactly. Separately (real but NOT the explanation for this error at context_length=115, where KV bytes are negligible next to a 2B model's weight bytes): found that youtu_llm.py's Attention decompresses compressed_kv via kv_b_proj BEFORE calling cache.update_and_fetch, caching the full per-head K/V rather than the compressed latent -- unlike mlx_lm.models.deepseek_v3.py's DeepseekV3Attention, confirmed by reading its source, which caches kv_latent/k_pe (the compressed form) and defers the kv_b_proj up-projection into the attention score computation itself, the real MLA inference-efficiency trick. This means this project's KV-cache-size assumption for MLA (kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim, shared not per-head) is correct for DeepSeek-V3-style implementations but WRONG for youtu_llm-style ones -- a real per-model_type implementation difference invisible from config.json fields alone (both declare the same kv_lora_rank/qk_rope_head_dim fields), not yet actionable as a fix (only one example of the 'decompressed' variant found so far, and it doesn't matter at short context) but relevant to this project's own long-context degradation claims for any youtu_llm-style MLA model. Not added to the 9-point speed-formula calibration set.
